evidence: src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp:377 constructs `meta_pool` (a bounded `ThreadPool`) and CasGc.cpp:417 schedules per-hash freshness-meta ops onto it via `meta_pool->scheduleOrThrowOnError(run)`; CasGc.h:876 documents 'Submit one per-hash freshness-meta op (condemn/spare/delete) to the bounded `meta_pool`', matching the claim that mass metadata operations require a bounded parallel pool rather than one-at-a-time CASes.

At HEAD GC condemns via `writeCondemnedMeta` (src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp:127-136) and drops meta after exact-token delete via `deleteConfirmedMeta` (CasGc.cpp:142), but a spare does NOT clear meta: CasGc.cpp:904 explicitly states 'A spare does NOT touch the meta. GC freshness meta is add-only -- GC never publishes `Clean`... the meta stays `Condemned`... until a WRITER displaces the body with a fresh incarnation token'. The claimed 'clears it at spare' transition was removed; the sole Condemned->Clean transition is now writer-side (`PartWriteTxn::uploadFromSource` + `writeResurrectMetaClean`), so this describes a superseded design.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp:139 explicitly documents 'NO tombstone -- an absent meta reads exactly like a Clean one', and the delete argument (CasGc.cpp:802, 1193, 1243, 3462, 3566) is the exact-token `deleteExact` model, not a 'won tombstone claim' -- there is no tombstone-claim-winning mechanism in the current GC delete path (a rejected 'raw-body/tombstone' design per project history). The 404-during-fold half of the claim is accurate (CasGc.cpp:1313, 1429 'a GC fold never fails a round on a 404'), but the compound claim's tombstone premise contradicts HEAD.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasBlobInDegree.h:29 defines `RetiredEntry::token` as 'the exact incarnation token GC observed (exact-token delete)' -- the body's incarnation token, not a condemned-meta etag. GC also never CASes condemned->clean on a spare (see CasGc.cpp:904, 'A spare does NOT touch the meta'), contradicting the claim's spare-clears-meta step; the condemn write is `writeCondemnedMeta` (CasGc.cpp:127) which stores no etag into `RetiredEntry`.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp:934-954 (the `merge.replaced` / supersede handling) compares the CURRENT object TOKEN observed via HEAD against the STALE retired entry's token ('current object token differs from the retired entry -- resurrect replaced the incarnation'; `detail["superseded_token"]` carries the old TOKEN), not a meta etag. Meta etags (`lm->etag`) are used only inside `writeCondemnedMeta`/`deleteConfirmedMeta` (CasGc.cpp:134,147) for the meta's own CAS, unrelated to supersede detection.

src/Disks/DiskObjectStorage/MetadataStorages/ContentAddressed/Gc/CasGc.cpp:331-341 (`shouldDeferRound`) implements exactly three forcing factors -- `graduation_due` (destructive demand), `changed_shards >= fold_threshold`, and `rounds_since_last_fold >= fold_max_defer_rounds` (max defer age) -- with no separate 'ref-tail pressure' or `remove_namespace` forcing condition (remove_namespace only appears as ordinary fold cleanup handling, CasGc.cpp:1967). Moreover CasGc.cpp:705-712 shows a deferred round explicitly SUPPRESSES destructive work ('DEFER has no `FoldResult`, hence no complete global destructive verdict... suppression keeps both deletes and valid-page cursor progress at the same position'), contradicting 'a deferred round still replays the complete tail for destructive protection'.
